description: A blank sex means unknown, so those patients are dropped before grouping and before the mean is computed.

a.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then, for each sex (leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank or missing), average those patient-level figures. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
a.sql:
WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
         AVG(l.ALB) AS avg_alb,
         AVG(CASE WHEN l.`T-BIL` <> 0 THEN l.UN * 1.0 / l.`T-BIL` END) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
  WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> ''
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_stats AS (
  SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_alb) AS sex_alb, AVG(avg_ratio) AS sex_ratio
  FROM patient_stats
  GROUP BY SEX
),
mean_alb AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_alb) AS m FROM sex_stats
)
SELECT s.SEX AS sex,
       s.sex_alb AS avg_alb,
       s.sex_ratio AS avg_un_tbil_ratio,
       s.sex_alb - m.m AS diff_from_mean
FROM sex_stats s, mean_alb m
WHERE s.sex_alb > m.m;

b.request: Among patients with a recorded sex (blank-sex patients dropped before grouping), joining Laboratory to Patient on ID and dropping unmatched lab rows, average ALB per patient, then average those per sex, and average the per-test UN/T-BIL ratios per patient before averaging to sex level, then return each sex whose sex-level ALB average exceeds the mean of the sex-level ALB averages, with that ALB average, its UN/T-BIL average, and the unrounded difference from the mean
b.sql: WITH patient_stats AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, l.ID AS id, AVG(l.ALB) AS alb_avg, AVG(l.UN * 1.0 / l.`T-BIL`) AS un_tbil_avg FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY p.SEX, l.ID), sex_stats AS (SELECT sex, AVG(alb_avg) AS alb_avg, AVG(un_tbil_avg) AS un_tbil_avg FROM patient_stats GROUP BY sex), overall AS (SELECT AVG(alb_avg) AS mean_alb FROM sex_stats) SELECT s.sex, s.alb_avg, s.un_tbil_avg, s.alb_avg - o.mean_alb AS diff_from_mean FROM sex_stats s CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE s.alb_avg > o.mean_alb;

c.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then average those patient-level figures for each sex. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round. A blank sex means unknown, so those patients are dropped before grouping and before the mean is computed.
c.sql: WITH patient_level AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) AS avg_alb, AVG(CASE WHEN l.`T-BIL` <> 0 THEN 1.0 * l.UN / l.`T-BIL` END) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sex_level AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM patient_level GROUP BY SEX), mean_alb AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS m FROM sex_level) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb AS avg_alb, s.avg_ratio AS avg_un_tbil_ratio, s.avg_alb - m.m AS alb_diff_above_mean FROM sex_level s CROSS JOIN mean_alb m WHERE s.avg_alb > m.m;

d.request:
Rewrite the follow-up so it stands alone, drawing on the earlier task:

Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`, then average those patient-level figures for each sex, ignoring missing values (including ratios that can't be computed) and without rounding. Drop patients whose `SEX` is blank (unknown) before grouping and before computing the mean. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages, and for each such sex, what is its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean?
d.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.ALB,
         CASE WHEN l.`T-BIL` <> 0 THEN l.UN / l.`T-BIL` END AS ratio
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
  WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> ''
),
patient_level AS (
  SELECT ID, SEX, AVG(ALB) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
),
sex_level AS (
  SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_alb) AS sex_alb, AVG(avg_ratio) AS sex_ratio
  FROM patient_level
  GROUP BY SEX
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_alb) AS mean_alb FROM sex_level
)
SELECT s.SEX,
       s.sex_alb AS avg_alb,
       s.sex_ratio AS avg_un_tbil_ratio,
       s.sex_alb - o.mean_alb AS diff_above_mean
FROM sex_level s
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE s.sex_alb > o.mean_alb;
